reviewMethod: Independent visual reading of all 32 question-paper pages and PDF pages 1–32 of the combined Higher Level scheme (cover, contents, the Paper 1 scale table on page 4, the summary of allocations on page 5, annotation palette, every Paper 1 model solution and marking note, and the Paper 2 scale table). Each task boundary is the published scale beside its model solution, cross-checked against the printed summary.
sourceNotes: The 2021 paper was adjusted for COVID-19 (220 marks): candidates answer any four of Q1–6 (30 marks each) and any two of Q7–10 (50 marks each), so 380 marks are offered and 220 count. Every question is retained.
44 independently marked units, matching the printed summary of allocations on scheme page 5. Every part has its own scale; none are shared.

Before this review the deck held 43 of the 44 units. Q9(a)(i) (show that A = 75, 5C) had no card and is added. Seven cards had marking points garbled by the scheme text layer (stacked fractions and exponents read out of order, the two Q2(a) and Q3(a) method ladders merged into one, solution lines shipped instead of credit notes) and are re-quoted from the printed scheme, labelled by band and method. On the remaining cards, any “Full Credit (−1)” deduction welded onto a credit band is moved to the row note. All existing IDs are kept; prompts are restored from the paper and topics corrected as metadata.
The question booklet is LC003ALP100EV.pdf; its indexed scheme LC003ALP000EV.pdf is shared with Paper 2. All page references are PDF positions, which match the printed scheme page numbers.

cards.stem: Trees of the same age, size and type are growing at the same rate in a forest. It is possible to measure the radius of the trunk of a tree at the end of each growing season. The increase in the radius of the trunks of these trees each year, in cm, during a particular 10 year period can be modelled by the formula: I(t) = 1·5 + sin(πt/5), where 1 ≤ t ≤ 10 and t ∈ ℕ is measured in years. Therefore r(1) = r(0) + I(1), r(2) = r(1) + I(2), …, r(t + 1) = r(t) + I(t + 1), where r(t) is the radius of the trunk of the tree after t years and r(0) is the radius of the trunk of a tree at the beginning of year 1.
cards.questionText: In order for the model to be reasonable it must satisfy a number of conditions. One condition is written below: “The radius of the trees is increasing year on year.” Show that r(t) satisfies this condition.
